q: Over one week, a patient's daily walks added up to 34/12 miles. Which mixed number, written in simplest form, is equal to 34/12?
w: 34 ÷ 12 = 2 with a remainder of 10, so 34/12 = 2 10/12. Simplify the fraction part by dividing both terms by 2: 2 5/6.

n.0: 3 1/6 = 38/12. It rounds the quotient up to 3 and uses 36 - 34 = 2 as twelfths.
n.2: This halves the numerator of 10/12 but not the denominator, which changes the value.
n.3: 2 10/12 equals 34/12, but the fraction part is not in simplest form.

q: A pharmacy logs several refill rates as fractions. Which of these fractions is already written in simplest form?
w: 33 = 3 × 11 and 56 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 7. They share no common factor other than 1, so 33/56 is in simplest form.

n.0: 21 and 49 share a factor of 7: 21/49 = 3/7.
n.1: 45 and 63 share a factor of 9: 45/63 = 5/7.
n.3: 26 and 39 share a factor of 13: 26/39 = 2/3.

q: A nurse's checklist has 5/6 of its tasks done. Which fraction with a denominator of 42 is equivalent to 5/6?

n.2: 30/42 multiplies the numerator by 6, the old denominator, instead of by 7.

q: Write 84/36 as a mixed number in lowest terms.

n.2: 2 12/36 has the right value, but the stem asks for lowest terms and 12/36 still shares a factor of 12.

q: If 4/9 = x/63, what value of x makes the two fractions equivalent?
w: 63 ÷ 9 = 7, so the denominator was multiplied by 7. Multiply the numerator by 7 too: 4 × 7 = 28. Check by cross-multiplying: 4 × 63 = 252 and 9 × 28 = 252.

n.1: 36 multiplies the old numerator by the old denominator (4 × 9) instead of by the multiplier 7.
n.2: 7 is the multiplier (63 ÷ 9), not the new numerator; the numerator 4 still has to be multiplied by it.
n.3: 58 adds 54 to the numerator because 54 was added to the denominator; adding the same number does not keep the value.

q: A unit stocks 30 IV poles, and 12 are in use. Which fraction is equivalent to 12/30?
w: 12/30 simplifies by its GCF, 6, to 2/5. 14/35 also simplifies to 2/5 (divide both terms by 7). Check by cross-multiplying: 12 × 35 = 420 and 30 × 14 = 420.

n.0: 14/32 adds 2 to the top and the bottom; adding does not keep the value (14/32 = 7/16).
n.1: 4/6 divides 12 by 3 but 30 by 5; 4/6 = 2/3, not 2/5.
n.3: 6/10 divides 12 by 2 but 30 by 3; 6/10 = 3/5, not 2/5.

q: A clinic filled 63 of its 84 appointment slots. What fraction of the slots was filled, in lowest terms?

n.0: 7/12 divides 63 by 9 but 84 by 7; dividing the terms by different numbers changes the value.
n.1: 9/12 divides both terms by 7 only; 9 and 12 still share a factor of 3.
n.3: 21/28 divides both terms by 3 only; 21 and 28 still share a factor of 7.

q: Write 6 4/10 as an improper fraction in lowest terms.

n.2: 34/5 simplifies 4/10 to 2/5 but then adds the old numerator 4 instead of 2 (6 × 5 + 4).
n.3: 34/10 multiplies the whole number by the numerator and adds the denominator (6 × 4 + 10).

q: Four students each completed part of the same online module. The parts completed were 5/9, 4/7, 6/11 and 7/13. Which fraction of the module is greatest?
w: Convert to decimals: 4/7 ≈ 0.571, 5/9 ≈ 0.556, 6/11 ≈ 0.545, 7/13 ≈ 0.538. The greatest is 4/7. (Cross-multiplying 4/7 and 5/9 also works: 4 × 9 = 36 > 5 × 7 = 35.)

n.0: 5/9 ≈ 0.556, slightly less than 4/7 ≈ 0.571 (cross products 35 < 36).
n.1: 7/13 ≈ 0.538 is actually the least; a larger denominator does not mean a larger fraction.
n.2: 6/11 ≈ 0.545; its larger numerator and denominator do not make it larger.

q: A nursing student records four lab values as 5/8, 0.6, 7/12 and 0.62. Which list is in order from least to greatest?

q: A dietitian records the fraction of a daily sodium limit in four meals as 4/9, 0.449, 7/16 and 0.44. Which value is the least?
w: Convert to decimals: 4/9 = 0.4444..., 0.449 = 0.4490, 7/16 = 0.4375 and 0.44 = 0.4400. Comparing place by place, 0.4375 is the least, so 7/16 is the least.

q: A pharmacy technician needs a value that is greater than 1/3 but less than 3/8. Which value lies between 1/3 and 3/8?

q: Four race times, in minutes, are listed in different forms. Which list shows the times in descending order (greatest to least)?

q: Four tablet strengths, in milligrams, are 0.125, 0.12, 0.2 and 0.1205. Which strength is the least?
w: Pad to four places: 0.1250, 0.1200, 0.2000 and 0.1205. Compare from the left: 0.1200 is the least, so 0.12 mg is the least.

n.2: 0.1205 has more digits but is greater than 0.1200 by 5 ten-thousandths.
n.3: 0.2 has the fewest digits, but 0.2000 is the greatest of the four; fewer digits do not mean a smaller value.

q: Which list orders 2/3, 3/5, 5/8 and 7/12 from greatest to least?

q: Four IV bags have 5/7, 0.71, 0.705 and 7/10 of their volume left. Which amount is greatest?
w: Convert and pad to four places: 5/7 = 0.7142..., 0.71 = 0.7100, 0.705 = 0.7050 and 7/10 = 0.7000. The greatest is 5/7.

q: Four bandage rolls measure 2 3/8, 2.4, 2 5/12 and 2.38 meters. Which roll is longest?

q: A patient drank 2/3 cup of juice at breakfast and 3/4 cup of juice at lunch. How many cups of juice did the patient drink in all?

q: A roll of medical tape held 6 1/4 yards. A nurse used 2 3/4 yards while dressing wounds during a shift. How many yards of tape are left on the roll?
w: 1/4 is less than 3/4, so borrow 1 from 6: 6 1/4 = 5 5/4. Then 5 5/4 - 2 3/4 = 3 2/4 = 3 1/2 yards.

n.2: 5 comes from borrowing 1 as 10/4 instead of 4/4 (5 11/4 - 2 3/4 = 3 8/4 = 5).

q: A 5-pound bag of flour is used for a community health kitchen. One recipe uses 1 5/6 pounds and another uses 2 3/8 pounds. How many pounds of flour are left in the bag?

q: A patient is to drink 3/5 of a 1 1/4-liter bottle of oral rehydration solution. How many liters should the patient drink?

q: A pharmacy technician has dispensed 3/8 of the tablets in a full stock bottle. Which percentage of the tablets in the bottle has been dispensed?

q: At lunch a patient is served a 480 mL nutritional shake and a 240 mL cup of juice. She drinks 300 mL of the shake and all of the juice. What percent of the total fluid served did she drink?
